title: OPF Set
description: Schema for set.json, an Open Practice Format (OPF) set, version 0.2.0. A set is an ordered collection of question references (see OQF) plus set-level metadata.

$schema.description: Optional. Points an editor (e.g. VS Code) at this document's JSON Schema for inline validation/autocomplete. A JSON-tooling convention, not part of the OES content model — an OES parser ignores it like any other unrecognized field.

opf_version.description: Any 0.2.x patch release of OPF — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

status.description: Content lifecycle stage. Absent is equivalent to "published" — this field exists for a consumer that wants to hide draft/deprecated content or an author's own tooling, not to gate access by itself.

questions.description: An ordered sequence of entries. Each is either a direct reference to one question, or a pool entry that a consumer expands into `select` randomly-chosen questions from `from` at attempt-assembly time — the two can be freely mixed and ordered, e.g. a few fixed questions, then a pool, then more fixed questions.

id.description: Stable identifier for this entry within the set. For a direct reference, must match the question's folder name when `path` points to a folder; no such constraint when `path` points directly to a single-file question.json, when using question_url, or for a pool entry.

title.description: Optional display label, mainly useful for question_url entries so a consumer can render a table of contents without fetching every question first.

path.description: Path, relative to set.json, to a question co-located within this set's own repo. Mutually exclusive with question_url and with select/from. Two shapes: a path ending in ".json" points directly to a single-file question (a lone question.json with an inline statement, no folder needed); any other path is a folder, resolved as "{path}/question.json" (the traditional shape, for a question that also has its own statement.md and/or assets/).

question_url.description: Absolute URL to a question.json hosted in a separate, independently-owned repo (e.g. a shared question bank). Mutually exclusive with path and with select/from.

content_hash.description: Optional sha256 hash of the referenced question.json, formatted "sha256-{hex}" — e.g. `"sha256-" + sha256hex(fileBytes)`. Meaningful mainly with question_url: lets a consumer detect when a shared/external question has changed since this set last pinned it (integrity, caching, and reproducible grading), the same way Subresource Integrity works on the web. Only meaningful alongside question_url; omit for co-located path references, which are already versioned by the set's own repo history.

points.description: How much this entry is worth in this particular set. For a pool entry, this is the per-question value applied uniformly to every question the pool selects, not a total. Not a property of the question itself — see OQF.

select.description: Marks this entry as a pool instead of a direct reference: at attempt-assembly time, a consumer randomly picks this many questions from `from` in place of this one entry. MUST be less than or equal to the length of `from` — not enforceable by schema alone, since it's a cross-field/cross-array constraint; see the Versioning & Conformance page's note on what schema validation does and doesn't catch.

shuffle.description: Only meaningful on a pool entry. If true (the default), the selected questions' presentation order is randomized on each assembly; if false, they're presented in `from`'s relative order.

from.description: Only meaningful on a pool entry: the candidate questions it selects from. Same reference shape as a direct entry (id + path|question_url + optional content_hash), minus points and title — a pool's own `points` applies uniformly to whichever questions get selected, and a pool has no per-candidate display label since only the selected subset is ever shown.

path.description: Path, relative to set.json, to a question co-located within this set's own repo. Mutually exclusive with question_url.

question_url.description: Absolute URL to a question.json hosted in a separate, independently-owned repo. Mutually exclusive with path.

source.description: Where this set was originally sourced or adapted from, if it wasn't authored directly for OES — e.g. produced by an importer against another platform's question bank. Entirely optional; omit for content authored directly. Distinct from this document's own top-level `license`, which describes this OES document's license, not what it was adapted from — the original may be more restrictive (or simply different) and belongs in `source.license` instead.

platform.description: Free-text label for the originating platform or site, e.g. "Khan Academy", "MIT OpenCourseWare". Deliberately not an enum — OES doesn't hard-code or endorse any specific platform; any importer fills in whatever's accurate.

license.description: The ORIGINAL content's license or terms of use at the source. Free text, not constrained to SPDX like this document's own `license` field — many platforms' terms of use aren't expressible as a single SPDX identifier.

retrieved_at.description: When this content was fetched/adapted from the source — provenance, and a signal for how stale this copy might be.

note.description: Free-text context an importer or author wants to record — adaptation details, attribution requirements, anything not covered by the fields above.
